_note: Starting content from the St Jude prototype. Facility staff must review every entry against local SOPs before relying on it.

severities.label: Stop now
severities.desc: Instrument or specimen may be at risk

resolution_types: Stopped on its own, cause unknown

problem_areas.label: Autoloader, cassette or grid transfer
hold: Pause the automated run. Do not repeat a failed load, dock or transfer command more than once.
Do not vent, open hatches, or touch the autoloader or dewars.
Leave the system in its current state. Staff will decide how to recover.
record: Exact error text and the time
Cassette position and grid slot involved
A photo or screenshot of the status screen

symptoms.label: Cassette will not dock or undock
Wrong or missing grid after load
Autoloader LN2 or temperature warning
Grid stuck or dropped during transfer

problem_areas.label: Cryo-holder or side-entry insertion
general: Leave the holder where it is. Do not pull it out or push it further in while the airlock is cycling.
Note the holder temperature, the holder dewar LN2 level and the vacuum reading shown.
avoid: Do not force the holder or rotate it beyond the position your training shows.
Do not warm up or remove a cryo-holder from the column unless staff tell you to.
record: The step you were on (pre-pump, insertion, imaging, removal)

symptoms.label: Airlock will not pump or holder will not go in
steps: Check the holder is seated straight in the airlock and the O-ring looks clean and undamaged.
Wait for the full pre-pump time shown on screen before turning the holder.
If the pre-pump does not finish after two attempts, leave the holder in the airlock position and call staff.

symptoms.label: Holder temperature is rising
steps: Check the holder dewar still has LN2. Top it up only if your training covers it.
Close the column valves to protect the specimen and the column.
Call staff now if the temperature keeps rising.

symptoms.label: Image vibrates or drifts with the holder in
steps: Check nothing is touching the holder dewar or its cable, and the LN2 is not boiling hard after a top-up.
Wait five to ten minutes after a top-up for the holder to settle, then check drift again.
If drift stays high, note the values for staff.

symptoms.label: Column vacuum dropped after insertion
steps: Close the column valves if they are not already closed.
Do not remove the holder. Call staff now.

problem_areas.label: Vacuum, LN2 level or temperature alarm
hold: Stop acquisition. Leave the column valves and the screen as they are.
Do not clear alarms or restart the microscope computer or server.
Do not refill or change LN2 yourself unless you are trained and the SOP says to.
record: Gauge or value shown, if any
What was happening when it appeared

symptoms.label: Column or gun vacuum alarm
LN2 level or refill alarm
Cryo temperature out of range

problem_areas.label: Beam, illumination or alignments
general: Confirm you are on the intended preset (magnification, spot size, C2 intensity) and nothing was changed after the last alignment.
Confirm the column valves are open and the screen is raised.
Compare with the facility daily-alignment record. Only redo alignments your training covers.
avoid: Do not adjust gun settings, the C2 aperture or the objective aperture unless you are trained and authorized.

symptoms.label: No beam or beam far off-center
steps: Confirm the column valves are open and the viewing screen is raised.
Check spot size, C2 intensity and magnification against your preset, and return to the preset if they changed.
Check that the beam is not blanked and that no aperture or beam stop is inserted, using the status indicators in the microscope interface.
If the beam is still missing, stop. Do not move apertures or gun settings.

symptoms.label: Beam not round, or it walks when intensity changes
steps: Look at the beam at your acquisition spot size and magnification. Is it elliptical, or does it shift as you change intensity?
Re-run condenser astigmatism and beam-shift pivot-point alignments only if your facility training covers them.
If values moved a lot from the last daily-alignment entry, note the numbers for staff.

symptoms.label: Suspected beam tilt or coma (asymmetric Thon rings)
steps: Acquire a short test exposure on thin ice or carbon at your usual dose and defocus.
Inspect the Fourier transform for asymmetric or elliptical Thon rings and run a quick CTF fit.
Compare with a reference exposure from the last staff-verified alignment, if one exists.
If the rings are asymmetric, ask staff to check coma-free alignment before collecting more.

symptoms.label: Dose rate unstable or different from expected
steps: Measure the dose rate over an empty hole. Note the value, spot size and C2 aperture in use.
Measure again after a few minutes. A steady offset points to a settings change. A continuing drift points to source or beam stability, which is a staff matter.
Change exposure time or dose rate in your protocol only after the value is stable.

problem_areas.label: Stage, eucentric height, focus or tilt tracking
general: Note the position, tilt angle and time when it started.
Compare the same behavior at a second position to separate a local problem from a global one.
avoid: Do not restart the stage controller or microscope server in the middle of a run.

symptoms.label: Image drift or smeared images after stage moves
steps: Wait for the stage to settle, then read the drift value in your software at the same position at two time points.
If drift falls with time, add a longer settling delay. If it stays high, move to a different grid square and compare.

High drift in only some squares points to the specimen or grid (for example buckling or an unsupported film). High drift everywhere points to the instrument, or to a recent thermal disturbance such as a cassette load.
If drift stays high everywhere, report the drift values and positions to staff.

symptoms.label: Eucentric height failure
steps: Note where it failed: the position, the magnification used for the routine, and the message or value shown.
Repeat the routine once on a flat, intact square, away from grid bars, broken squares and thick ice. Do not run it repeatedly.
Check that the routine has something with contrast to follow. An empty hole or featureless ice gives it nothing to track.
Check the result by tilting a few degrees the way your SOP does. A recognizable feature that stays in place means the height is right. One that walks sideways means it is off.

Run the routine on two or three neighboring squares and compare the heights. A large jump between neighbors points to an uneven or buckled grid or clip. A steady offset on every square points to the stage or its calibration, which is a staff matter.
On the cryo-FIB, confirm the stage is at the position your protocol uses before repeating the routine.
If the height sits at the limit of the stage range, or the routine fails on every grid, stop and call staff. Note the z values you saw.

symptoms.label: Autofocus failing
steps: Check that the autofocus target area is on ice or carbon, not on a grid bar or an empty hole.
Check the autofocus tolerance and defocus range in your protocol. Very tight tolerances can cause repeated retries.
Check that eucentric height was set at this position, since a wrong height often shows up as failing autofocus.
If the focus value sits at the limit of the lens range, stop and call staff.

symptoms.label: Tilt-series tracking lost (cryo-ET)
steps: Open the series and find the tilt angle where tracking failed.
Check that the tracking and focus area sits on the lamella or specimen, not on a gap, edge or grid bar, especially at high tilt.
Check that the pretilt setting matches the lamella or grid orientation as loaded.
If it fails at similar angles at different positions, increase the tracking exposure within your dose budget.
If the stage itself errors at high tilt, stop and call staff.

problem_areas.label: Detector, gain reference or frame saving
general: Check the camera status in the camera software: inserted or retracted, ready, and connected.
Acquire one short test exposure in a plain area to see whether it completes.
avoid: Do not restart the camera server or acquisition computer in the middle of a run without asking staff.
Do not delete or move existing frames.

symptoms.label: Camera not ready, not inserting or not acquiring
steps: Check the camera status in the camera software: inserted or retracted, ready, and connected.
Check that the acquisition software shows the camera as connected, and note the exact message.
Acquire one short test exposure in a plain area.
If the test fails, ask staff.

symptoms.label: Streaks, fixed-pattern noise or an old gain reference
steps: Note the date of the gain reference currently in use.
Acquire a no-specimen exposure and look for streaks, lines or fixed patterns.
Acquire a second exposure. A pattern that repeats points to the detector or reference. A pattern that changes points to the specimen or beam.
If the pattern repeats, ask staff whether a new gain reference is due.

symptoms.label: Frames not saving, missing files or disk errors
steps: Check free space on the acquisition drive and the destination storage.
Check that the destination folder is reachable: share mounted, permissions in place.
Check that frame format and number of fractions match your protocol and your processing plan.
Note the last micrograph that saved correctly and the time of the first failure.

problem_areas.label: Energy filter or slit
general: Confirm the slit is inserted at the width set in your protocol.

symptoms.label: Zero-loss peak drifting or off-center
steps: Confirm the slit is inserted at the width set in your protocol.
Re-center the zero-loss peak in an empty hole following the facility procedure and note the shift.
Check again after a while. A large repeated shift tells staff the filter is drifting.

symptoms.label: Low or uneven intensity with the slit in
steps: Compare intensity with the slit retracted at the same spot size and exposure.
Check that the slit is centered on the zero-loss peak and not offset.
If the image is uneven even when centered, ask staff to check filter tuning.

symptoms.label: Filter tuning fails
steps: Note the error message and which tuning step failed.
Do not repeat the tuning more than once. Ask staff.

problem_areas.label: Acquisition software (EPU, SerialEM, Tomo5)
general: Take a screenshot of the status or error and note the time.
Check the software log for the last error line and report it to staff.
avoid: Pause rather than stop where possible, so your position queue stays intact where the software allows.

symptoms.label: Acquisition stalls or is stuck on one step
steps: Take a screenshot of the status and note the time.
Check whether the camera, stage and microscope connections all show as responsive.
Compare with how long the same step took earlier in this session.
Pause rather than stop where possible.
Check the software log for the last error line and report it to staff.

symptoms.label: Hole or square finding fails (EPU)
steps: Check that atlas and square registration look correct on the map.
Check that hole size and spacing in the template match the grid in use.
Check ice-thickness or contrast filter thresholds. If they are too strict, most holes are rejected.
Test on a few holes manually before restarting the run.

symptoms.label: Script or Navigator error (SerialEM)
steps: Read the last lines in the SerialEM log window and note which script line failed.
Check that calibrations exist for the magnification, spot size and mode in use.
After a cassette re-dock or grid reload, check that Navigator items still register to the stage coordinates, and re-register if needed.
If the script worked earlier in this session, note what changed since then.

problem_areas.label: Ice, contamination or grid quality
general: Compare several squares across the grid before deciding it is a whole-grid problem.
Record grid slot and squares examined so staff and your lab can follow up.

symptoms.label: Ice too thick
steps: Compare ice thickness across squares using the atlas or square images and choose thinner squares.
If your software has an ice-thickness or contrast filter, apply it to select holes.
If the whole grid is thick, move to the next grid and note it for your next grid preparation.

symptoms.label: Crystalline ice or contamination
steps: Check whether the contamination is on one square, the whole grid, or all grids.
If it is grid-specific, choose clean squares or another grid.
If it appears on every grid and grows during the session, stop and tell staff. That can point to the instrument rather than the specimen.

symptoms.label: Few or no particles, or aggregation
steps: Look at a few holes in several squares to see whether distribution changes with ice thickness.
Acquire a handful of test micrographs and inspect them at full resolution.
If particles gather at hole edges or aggregate, treat it as a sample or grid-preparation issue. Screening another grid may be faster than adjusting acquisition.

symptoms.label: Beam-induced motion or charging
steps: Look at the motion traces of the first frames across several micrographs.
Compare holes at the center and edge of a square, and different squares.
If motion is high at the start of the exposure everywhere, ask staff about dose rate and exposure options.

symptoms.label: Broken squares or cracked grid
steps: Check the atlas for how many squares are intact.
Compare with another grid from the same batch if you have one.
If squares broke after loading, record the grid slot and tell staff in case it happened during transfer.

problem_areas.label: Data quality (CTF, motion, resolution)
general: Run motion correction and CTF estimation on the first 50 to 100 micrographs.
Plot CTF fit resolution, astigmatism, and measured defocus against your target defocus range.

Split the results three ways: by grid square, by acquisition time, and by hole position. A square-specific problem points to the specimen. A time-dependent one points to drift or ice build-up. A uniform problem points to the instrument or setup.
Share the plots and the pattern you found with staff.

symptoms.label: Poor CTF fits
High total motion
Resolution limit lower than expected
Defocus far from target
steps: Check the defocus range and autofocus settings in your protocol.
Check eucentric height at the acquisition positions.
Plot measured defocus along the hole-to-hole acquisition path to see where it departs from target.

problem_areas.label: Shuttle, autoloader or sample transfer
hold: Stop. Do not repeat the transfer, docking or loading step.
Leave the shuttle, rod and chamber in their current state.
Keep the loading station topped up with LN2 if you are trained to, so samples stay cold.
record: The exact step and error message
Which shuttle position or cassette slot
A photo of the screen and the loading station

symptoms.label: Shuttle or transfer rod stuck
Autoloader or cassette will not dock (Arctis)
Loading station LN2 or frost problem
Grid fell out or clip ring damaged

problem_areas.label: Lamella milling
general: Pause milling and do not start the next step until the problem is clear.
Save the current positions and record the milling step, current and pattern you were on.
avoid: Do not change beam currents or retract the stage while a lamella is at risk without asking staff.

symptoms.label: Lamella cracks or breaks
steps: Pause milling. Note the step (rough milling, fine milling, polishing) and angle when the damage appeared.
Image the lamella and surrounding area, and save the image with the position.
Check whether other lamellae on the grid show the same pattern. If so, the cause may be grid-wide (ice thickness, grid mounting) rather than the milling.
Tell staff before starting more lamellae with the same parameters.

symptoms.label: Lamella thickness not as expected
steps: Record your current thickness estimate and the method you used.
Check milling currents, pattern sizes and milling angle against your protocol.
Check for redeposition or ice contamination on the surface.
Change one parameter at a time and tell staff what you changed.

symptoms.label: Ice contamination on the lamella
steps: Note when the contamination appeared relative to milling and imaging.
Compare with another lamella on the same grid and with other grids from this session.
If contamination builds on every sample, ask staff to check the chamber and cold trap.

problem_areas.label: SEM or ion-beam imaging
general: Save an image of the problem with the beam settings in the data bar.
Check whether the problem is on every grid and position or only this one.
avoid: Do not change source, gun or plasma-gas settings unless you are trained for them.

symptoms.label: Charging, drift or unstable imaging
steps: Check that the sample has the conductive (sputter or GIS) layer your protocol calls for.
Compare image stability at a lower voltage or current.
If drift is at every position, ask staff to check shuttle and clip seating.

symptoms.label: No SEM or ion-beam image
steps: Check that the beam is on, unblanked and the correct detector is selected.
Check the chamber vacuum is ready and the stage is not at a blocked position.
If the beam still does not appear, stop and call staff.

symptoms.label: Ion beam current wrong or drifting (plasma FIB)
steps: Measure the current in the Faraday cup if your training covers it, and note the value.
Compare with the value for this aperture in your protocol.
Pause milling until staff confirm the current. Wrong currents can destroy lamellae.

symptoms.label: SEM and FIB images do not line up (coincidence)
steps: Re-check eucentric height on a clear feature.
Set the coincidence point again following your SOP.
If it will not hold, note the stage position and call staff.

problem_areas.label: GIS or sputter coating
general: Note which coating step failed and the settings used (time, temperature, current).
avoid: Do not repeat a deposition more than once. Thick layers can ruin the lamella site.

symptoms.label: No platinum (GIS) layer deposited
steps: Image the surface to see whether any layer was deposited.
Check the GIS needle inserted and the heater reached temperature.
Ask staff to check the GIS before continuing.

symptoms.label: Sputter coating fails or is uneven
steps: Note the sputter current and time you used.
Check the shuttle was in the sputter position.
Ask staff before coating again.

problem_areas.label: Automation software (AutoTEM, Maps, WebUI)
general: Take a screenshot of the error and note the time and the site name.
Save the current sites and positions before trying anything else.
avoid: Do not delete sites or projects to clear an error.

symptoms.label: Automated milling stalls or skips sites
steps: Check which step the queue stopped on and whether that site was marked as failed.
Pause the queue rather than stopping it, so the remaining sites keep their state.
Report the step and the site to staff.

symptoms.label: Image recognition or alignment fails
steps: Check the reference image is sharp and taken at the right magnification.
Retake the reference image once, then retry the site.
If it fails on every site, ask staff.

symptoms.label: Software crashed or will not connect to the microscope
steps: Do not restart the microscope server.
Note whether the microscope user interface still responds.
Call staff to restart the software safely.

problem_areas.label: Lift-out or micromanipulator needle
general: Retract the needle to its park position only if your training covers it.
avoid: Do not drive the needle near the sample while it is not tracking correctly.

symptoms.label: Needle bent, broken or contaminated
steps: Image the needle tip and save the image.
Retract the needle and tell staff before another lift-out.

symptoms.label: Chunk will not attach or release
steps: Note the attach method (redeposition, GIS, cryo-condensation) and the step.
Try once more following your SOP, then ask staff.

symptoms.label: Needle will not move or moves the wrong way
steps: Stop moving the needle.
Call staff to check the manipulator.

problem_areas.label: Humidity or chamber temperature
general: Note the humidity and temperature set points and the values shown now.
Check the humidifier water container is filled with the water your SOP says (usually distilled).
avoid: Do not open the humidifier or chamber electronics.

symptoms.label: Humidity will not reach the set point
steps: Refill the humidifier water if it is low.
Close the chamber door fully and wait five minutes.
Check the humidifier is switched on in the settings.
If it is still low, keep the instrument on and call staff.

symptoms.label: Water dripping or condensation in the chamber
steps: Lower the humidity to 90% and wait for it to settle.
Dry visible water with lint-free tissue if it is safe to reach.
Tell staff if water keeps collecting.

symptoms.label: Chamber temperature wrong
steps: Compare the set point and the reading.
Allow 15 minutes after start-up for the temperature to settle.
Report the readings to staff if it does not settle.

problem_areas.label: Blotting or ice thickness
general: Note blot force, blot time, wait time and the filter paper you used.
Change one setting at a time and make a test grid.

symptoms.label: Blot pads not touching or uneven
steps: Check the filter paper is mounted flat and fully clipped on both pads.
Replace filter paper that is wet, torn or creased.
If the pads still do not close evenly, ask staff to check the blot arms.

symptoms.label: Filter paper tears or falls off
steps: Use fresh filter paper of the type your SOP lists.
Make sure the paper is punched to fit the pads.
Tell staff if the clips or rings are loose.

symptoms.label: Ice too thick, too thin or uneven
steps: Too thick: increase blot time or force by one step. Too thin or empty: decrease it.
Check the humidity was at the set point when you blotted.
Check your sample volume and glow-discharge time.
Keep notes of the settings that worked for your lab.

problem_areas.label: Ethane, LN2 or cryogen container
general: Work in the ventilated area and keep ignition sources away from ethane.
Wear the eye and hand protection your SOP requires.
avoid: Do not leave a condensing ethane line unattended.
Do not add ethane to warm containers or pour LN2 into the ethane cup.

symptoms.label: Ethane will not condense
steps: Check the outer container is full of LN2 and has cooled for at least five minutes.
Check the ethane cylinder valve is open and the regulator shows pressure.
If the cylinder is empty, close it and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Ethane froze solid
steps: Lift the ethane cup slightly above the LN2, or wait for the warmer to work, so it melts.
Do not plunge into solid or slushy ethane.

symptoms.label: Smell of gas or a leaking line
steps: Close the ethane cylinder valve if it is safe to do so.
Move away, keep sparks and flames away, and call staff now.

symptoms.label: LN2 boils off too fast or no LN2 available
steps: Check the container lid and foam are in place.
Check the facility LN2 dewar level and tell staff if it is low.

problem_areas.label: Tweezers, plunger or grid handling
general: Note the step where it went wrong (mounting, blotting, plunging, transfer to the grid box).
avoid: Do not put fingers under the plunger while it is armed.

symptoms.label: Tweezers will not lock or hold the grid
steps: Check you are using the tweezers made for this instrument.
Check the tweezer tips are straight and close evenly.
Tell staff if the tweezer mount is loose.

symptoms.label: Plunger does not fire or stops halfway
steps: Check the chamber door is closed and the cryogen container is in position.
Restart the plunge sequence once from the start screen.
If it fails again, leave the instrument and call staff.

symptoms.label: Grids bent or lost during transfer
steps: Pre-cool tweezers before touching the grid in the ethane.
Check the grid box and holder are under LN2 and in the right position.
Tell staff if grids bend on every plunge.

problem_areas.label: Chamber will not pump down or vent
general: Check the chamber lid or door is seated and the O-ring is clean.
Note the pressure shown and how long you waited.
avoid: Do not force the lid open while the chamber is under vacuum.

symptoms.label: Pump-down is slow or never reaches the set point
steps: Vent, wipe the O-ring with lint-free tissue, reseat the lid and pump again.
Remove anything wet or outgassing (tape, damp filter paper) from the chamber.
If it still does not pump down, tell staff.

symptoms.label: Chamber will not vent
steps: Check the vent gas supply is on, if your instrument uses one.
Wait two minutes and try venting again from the controls.
Call staff if the lid stays locked.

problem_areas.label: Glow discharge or plasma cleaning
general: Note gas, current or power, and time used.

symptoms.label: No glow, or glow flickers
steps: Check the chamber reached the required vacuum before starting.
Check the gas supply (air, argon, oxygen or hydrogen) is open and not empty.
Try once more. If there is still no glow, tell staff.

symptoms.label: Grids not hydrophilic after treatment
steps: Test with a drop of water on a treated grid. It should spread flat.
Use grids within 30 minutes of treatment.
Increase time or power one step, then tell staff if it still fails.

problem_areas.label: Carbon or metal coating
general: Note the coating mode, target thickness and the thickness reading at the end.
avoid: Do not touch the carbon rod, thread or target while it is hot.

symptoms.label: No coating, or the carbon thread breaks
steps: Check a carbon thread or rod is fitted and has not run out.
Replace the thread if you are trained, following the SOP.
Tell staff if the source does not heat.

symptoms.label: Thickness reading looks wrong
steps: Check the quartz-crystal monitor is not at the end of its life (shown on the controls).
Compare with a test coat on a slide or grid.
Tell staff the reading and what you expected.

symptoms.label: Coating uneven or flaking
steps: Check the sample stage was rotating or tilting as set.
Check the sample was clean and dry before coating.
Tell staff if the problem repeats.

problem_areas.label: UV lamp, timer or ozone
general: Note the cleaning time you set and how long the lamp was on.
Let the unit cool for a few minutes before opening it after a run.
avoid: Do not look at the lamp while it is on, and do not defeat the door interlock.
Do not open the unit straight after a run: let the ozone clear first.

symptoms.label: Lamp does not switch on
steps: Check the door is fully closed; most cleaners will not start with it open.
Check the timer is set and the unit is switched on at the wall.
Try once more. If the lamp still does not light, tell staff.

symptoms.label: Timer or door interlock not working
steps: Note what the display shows.
Do not run the lamp with the door open or the interlock bypassed.
Label the unit "Do not use" and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Ozone smell outside the unit
steps: Switch the unit off and keep the door closed.
Ventilate the room and step away if the smell is strong.
Tell staff now.

symptoms.label: Grids not hydrophilic after cleaning
steps: Test with a drop of water on a cleaned grid. It should spread flat.
Use grids soon after cleaning; the effect fades within hours.
Increase the cleaning time one step, then tell staff if it still fails.

problem_areas.label: LN2 supply or freezing pressure
hold: Stop freezing. Leave the instrument powered on.
Do not open covers or the LN2 supply line.
record: How many shots you had done

symptoms.label: Freezing pressure not reached
LN2 level or supply alarm
LN2 or pressure leak

problem_areas.label: Sample carriers or loading
general: Note the carrier type and size, and the filler you used.
avoid: Do not use tools to force a carrier in or out.

symptoms.label: Carrier or cartridge jammed
steps: Stop and do not run the instrument again.
Call staff to free the cartridge.

symptoms.label: Sample lost or carrier empty after freezing
steps: Check the carriers are closed correctly and the sample fills the cavity.
Check the filler (hexadecene, BSA, yeast paste) matches your protocol.
Tell staff if carriers open during every shot.

symptoms.label: Poor freezing (ice crystals) in the sample
steps: Check the sample thickness is within the carrier depth.
Check the time between loading and freezing was short.
Share the pressure and cooling curves with staff, if the instrument shows them.

problem_areas.label: UV light or pattern projection
general: Note the objective, UV dose and the pattern used.
avoid: Do not look into the light path or remove covers.

symptoms.label: No UV light or the light source will not start
steps: Check the light source is switched on and has warmed up.
Check the shutter and the light path settings on the microscope.
Tell staff if it still does not start.

symptoms.label: Pattern out of focus or in the wrong place
steps: Focus on the grid surface with the same objective you will pattern with.
Re-run the calibration in the software if your training covers it.
Tell staff if the offset stays.

problem_areas.label: Patterning result (PLPP, protein binding)
general: Note the PLPP batch, the dose and the incubation times used.

symptoms.label: Patterns faint or missing
steps: Check the PLPP is within its use-by date and was kept dark.
Increase the dose one step on a test grid.
Tell staff the settings if it still fails.

symptoms.label: Cells or protein not sticking to the pattern
steps: Check the passivation and protein coating steps followed your protocol.
Check the grids did not dry out between steps.

problem_areas.label: Patterning software (Leonardo)
general: Take a screenshot of the error and note the time.

symptoms.label: Software crashes or will not see the microscope
steps: Save your pattern files.
Close and restart the software once.
Tell staff if the microscope still is not found.

symptoms.label: Licence or login error
steps: Note the exact message and tell staff.

problem_areas.label: Lasers or light source
general: Note which laser lines and channels you use.
avoid: Do not open laser covers or bypass interlocks.

symptoms.label: Laser will not switch on
steps: Check the laser power switch and key are on, in the order your SOP gives.
Check the laser is enabled in the software and has warmed up.
Tell staff which laser line is affected.

symptoms.label: Weak or no signal
steps: Check the correct objective, filters and detector are selected.
Check the laser power and gain against a sample that worked before.
Tell staff if a standard slide also gives weak signal.

symptoms.label: Transmitted or fluorescence lamp not working
steps: Check the lamp is switched on and the shutter is open.
Tell staff if the lamp does not light.

problem_areas.label: Image quality, focus or Airyscan processing
general: Save an example image with its settings.

symptoms.label: Image blurry or will not focus
steps: Clean the objective and use the right immersion medium.
Check the correction collar matches your coverslip, if the objective has one.
Check the sample is flat and the slide is the right way up.

symptoms.label: Airyscan processing fails or looks wrong
steps: Check the detector was aligned during acquisition (the hexagon view).
Process again with the default strength setting.
Tell staff the file name.

symptoms.label: Sample bleaches very fast
steps: Lower the laser power and increase gain.
Reduce the pixel dwell time or number of averages.

problem_areas.label: Stage, objectives or incubation
general: Note the objective and stage position.
avoid: Do not drive an oil objective across a dry sample, or the reverse.

symptoms.label: Stage will not move or is not calibrated
steps: Check nothing is blocking the stage or insert.
Calibrate the stage from the software if your training covers it.
Tell staff if it still will not move.

symptoms.label: Objective damaged, dirty or will not change
steps: Do not try to remove the objective.
Tell staff which objective position is affected.

symptoms.label: Incubation or cryo-stage temperature or CO2 wrong
steps: Compare the set point and the reading.
Allow the time your SOP gives for the chamber to settle.
Tell staff if it does not settle.

problem_areas.label: ZEN software or computer
general: Save your data and take a screenshot of the error.
avoid: Do not switch off hardware while the software is still running.

symptoms.label: Software crashed or froze
steps: Close the software, then restart it once, following the start-up order in your SOP.
Tell staff if it crashes again.

symptoms.label: Software does not find the microscope hardware
steps: Close the software, check the hardware is switched on in the right order, then restart.
Tell staff which component is missing.

problem_areas.label: Controls, display or error message
general: Take a photo of the screen or error message and note the time.
Note what you pressed just before the error.
avoid: Do not change instrument settings or calibrations you were not trained on.

symptoms.label: Error message on the screen
steps: Read the message and follow it only if it gives a simple user action (close door, refill water).
Otherwise leave the instrument as it is and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Instrument will not switch on or start
steps: Check the power switch and the socket.
Check any emergency stop or door interlock is released.
Tell staff if it still will not start.

symptoms.label: Screen frozen or not responding
steps: Wait one minute.
Restart the instrument once if your SOP allows it.
Tell staff if it freezes again.

problem_areas.label: Bench equipment (pipettes, centrifuge, fume hood)
general: Note the equipment name and what went wrong.
avoid: Do not use a fume hood whose airflow alarm is sounding.

symptoms.label: Equipment broken or not working
steps: Label it "Do not use" and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Bench left dirty or contaminated
steps: Do not clean up unknown spills. Tell staff what you see.

symptoms.label: Fume hood airflow alarm
steps: Close any open containers, lower the sash and step away.
Tell staff now.

problem_areas.label: Supplies or consumables running out
general: Check the spare supplies shelf or cabinet listed in your SOP.
Note what is missing and roughly how much is left.

symptoms.label: Grids, filter paper or tweezers
steps: Tell staff what is missing. Use another lab grid box only with permission.

symptoms.label: Gas cylinder, ethane or LN2 low
steps: Close the cylinder valve if it is empty, and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Stain, reagent or water
steps: Note the reagent and the lot number, and tell staff.

symptoms.label: Gloves, eye protection or other safety items
steps: Do not work without the protection your SOP requires.

problem_areas.label: Data transfer, storage or network
avoid: Do not delete, rename or move collected data until staff confirm it is safe.

symptoms.label: Disk almost full
steps: Check free space on the acquisition computer and on the storage target.
Estimate what the rest of the collection needs: movie size times micrographs still to come.
Tell staff the free space and the expected finish time so they can clear space or pause.

symptoms.label: Transfer stalled or share unreachable
steps: Check whether the transfer job or service is running and when it last moved files.
Check that the network share is reachable from the acquisition computer.
Leave source files in place until transfer is confirmed complete.

symptoms.label: Files missing or corrupted
steps: Note which micrographs or movies are affected and the time range.
Compare file sizes of good and bad files in the same folder.
Report the time of the first failure, since it helps staff correlate it with system events.

problem_areas.label: EMhub data transfer or data access
general: Write down your EMhub session or project name, the instrument, and the date of the collection.
Take a screenshot of what EMhub shows (missing session, wrong counts, error message) and note the time.
avoid: Do not rename or move session folders or files. The EMhub session record may refer to them by path.
Do not start the same transfer repeatedly. Wait for staff if the first attempt did not complete.

symptoms.label: Session or data not appearing in EMhub
steps: Confirm the collection has finished writing on the acquisition computer, or that the session is still running.
Check that the session is linked to the right project and instrument in EMhub.
Check that you are logged in with the account that owns the project.
Note the session name, the folder path where the data were written, and the time of the last file. Give these to staff.

symptoms.label: Transfer to EMhub-linked storage is stalled or slow
steps: Check whether the transfer job or service is running and when it last moved files.
Check free space at the destination storage and on the acquisition computer.
Check that the network share is reachable from the acquisition computer.
Leave the source files in place until the transfer is confirmed complete.

symptoms.label: File counts or sizes do not match
steps: Count the movies on the acquisition side and at the destination for the same session.
Compare file sizes of a few good and bad files in the same folder.
Note the time range of the missing or small files and report it to staff. It helps them correlate it with system events.

symptoms.label: Cannot open or download data from EMhub
steps: Check that you are logged in and that the project is listed under your account or lab.
Try a second browser or a private window to rule out a stale session.
Note the exact error text and the project name, and send both to staff.

problem_areas.label: EMhub booking or scheduling
general: Write down the instrument, date, time slot and booking name or ID involved.
Take a screenshot of the calendar or booking screen.
avoid: Do not create duplicate bookings to work around a problem. A duplicate can block the slot for other users.

symptoms.label: Cannot find or create a booking
steps: Check that you are logged in with your own account.
Check that the calendar is filtered to the right instrument and the right date range.
Check that your project or application is approved for that instrument. If you are unsure, ask staff.
Refresh the page, or try a second browser, then try once more.

symptoms.label: Booking conflict or overlapping sessions
steps: Compare your booking time with the neighboring bookings on the same instrument.
Note who holds the overlapping slot and the times involved.
Do not move or cancel anyone else's booking. Send the details to staff.

symptoms.label: Booking shows the wrong time, instrument or project
steps: Compare the booking with your confirmation or notes and note what differs.
Check the time zone and date display on the screen.
Do not edit the booking again until staff have seen it. Send a screenshot to staff.

symptoms.label: Cannot change or cancel a booking
steps: Check whether the booking is close to its start time, since some changes may be locked by facility rules.
Check that you are the owner of the booking.
Note the booking name or ID and what you tried, and send them to staff.

symptoms.label: Cannot log in or no instrument access
steps: Check that you are using the right account and address.
Check whether the problem is on one device only by trying a second device or browser.
Note the exact error text and send it to staff.

problem_areas.label: Something else or not sure
general: Write down what you saw, what you were doing, and the time.
Take a screenshot or photo of any message on screen.
If you are unsure whether it is safe to continue, pause and wait for staff.
